messages:
support-oncall: FYI customer com-475 opened an escalation — intermittent 400s from /v1/embeddings + periodic tail-latency spikes. They say errors say "dimension mismatch" even though payloads are consistent. Pasting summary and logs below.

support-oncall: customer timeline: high QPS small payloads (mostly short texts) from a few app servers -> 99th pct latency jumps to 2.8s; ~1% of calls get 400 with message: "Dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024". Started ~2026-03-15 14:03 UTC.

alice: Can you paste a sample failing request and the exact error from our side? Also customer says they pinned model to "embed-large-v1" — are there any fallbacks going on?

support-oncall: customer provided example body (abbreviated):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer sk_xxx
{
  "model": "embed-large-v1",
  "input": ["short sentence 1", "another short one"]
}
```
And our gateway log: 
```
[2026-03-15T14:12:03Z] req_id=abc123 route=/v1/embeddings model=embed-large-v1 status=400 err="Dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024"
[worker-node-7] batch_id=bn-77 batch_size=48 variants_in_batch=[embed-large-v1, embed-large-v1-quant]
```

ben: That batch log is the clue — variants_in_batch contains two different variants. The quantized variant returns 1024-dim embeddings. If batches mix variants we get client-visible mismatch. Why are variants being mixed? Our dynamic-batcher should key by model+variant.

carla: Checking routing rules — there was a recent config tweak to allow variant fallback for capacity (we call it "compatible-variant-fallthrough") for the embeddings family. It was intended to only apply at model-family level but looks like the batch-key was miscomputed and allowed mixing. I see recent deploy 2026-03-15T13:45 that touched batch-key hashing in router.

dave: Customer also reports tail latency spikes aligned with the 400s. Hypothesis: clients send many small requests which coalesce into medium-size batches; when a mixed-variant batch is sent to the quantized node, it produces 1024-dim outputs for the whole batch and some clients reject on validate -> we surface a 400 for those. The retry pattern then causes queue flapping and tail latency spikes.

support-oncall: Repro attempt (from our test cluster):
1) Run 200 short concurrent requests pinned to embed-large-v1
2) Observe batches forming with mixed variant ids when router hash is degraded
Command used:
```bash
seq 1 200 | xargs -n1 -P50 -I{} curl -s -X POST https://staging.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer test' -d '{"model":"embed-large-v1","input":["test"]}'
```
Observed: ~3% 400s with the same dimension mismatch message and 99p latency jumps.

alice: Good repro. Immediate mitigations:
- Turn off compatible-variant-fallthrough for embeddings route (fast rollback).
- Add a safety check in the batcher that rejects mixing variants in the same batch (short-term guard).
- Ask infra to roll back the batch-key change if that's the root.

carla: I can flip the route flag to disable fallthrough now. Also enabling an alert on batcher:variant_mismatch count > 0.

infra-bot: deploy:config-update by carla accepted — flag compatible-variant-fallthrough=false on route embeddings applied to prod-edge-pool-a,b at 2026-03-15T14:25:12Z :white_check_mark:

ben: Longer-term we should:
- Enforce batching key to include variant id (not just model family)
- Add unit/integration test that sends a mix of variant-ready tokens and assert batcher never merges them
- Consider returning 409 instead of 400 for variant mismatch so clients can better distinguish this from payload errors

dave: Customer asked about workarounds in the meantime. Suggested:
- Pin to dedicated pool (if they have Dedicated) or
- Add client-side retry with jitter and backoff; backoff reduces coalescing pressure.

support-oncall: Also noticed a secondary issue: some requests return 402 (billing) intermittently a few seconds before a dimension-mismatch incident. The sequence seems to be: a handful of requests rejected with 402 -> client retries -> retries pile up and change coalescing timing -> mixed batches more likely. Could be unrelated but worth checking the customer's billing quota window.

carla: I checked quota logs for com-475 — there were a couple of short-lived 402s due to a refresh race during token rotation on their side. Not our billing backend. But the retries certainly made the coalescing pattern worse.

alice: Action items:
- carla: roll back flag (done) and collect detailed batcher debug logs for window 14:00-14:30 UTC (please upload)
- ben: add variant key to batcher hashing and a unit test (P0 for batcher integrity)
- dave/support-oncall: coordinate with customer to resume normal traffic and ask them to stagger token refreshes for next 24h
- infra: monitor 99p latency and variant_mismatch counter for 6 hours

support-oncall: For reproducing locally for engineers: attached minimal python script (pasteable) to hammer staging with concurrency and print variations in response dims.
```python
import requests,concurrent.futures
URL='https://staging.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings'
HEADERS={'Authorization':'Bearer TEST'}
BODY={'model':'embed-large-v1','input':['x']}

def hit(i):
    r=requests.post(URL,json=BODY,headers=HEADERS,timeout=10)
    if r.status_code!=200:
        return (i,r.status_code,r.text[:200])
    j=r.json()
    dim=len(j['data'][0]['embedding'])
    return (i,200,dim)

with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=80) as ex:
    out=list(ex.map(hit,range(300)))
    print([o for o in out if o[1]!=200][:10])
```

carla: Uploaded batcher debug logs to S3: s3://redwood-support/dumps/6375550000-batcher-debug.log.gz

infra-bot: monitor:alert created: batcher.variant_mismatch > 0 for any route (window 5m) — notify @eng-runtime oncall

ben: I'll prioritize the batch-key bugfix and add a CI test. If anyone wants to pair on the fix ping me.

dave: I'll reply to the customer with status + workaround (disable client token burst, short retry+jitter), and let them know we've rolled back the fallthrough flag.

support-oncall: Closing loop: rollback reduced 400s to ~0.03% and 99p latency returned to baseline ~200ms. Keeping this thread open until ben's fix lands and we have post-mortem. :thumbsup:

carla: tagging for postmortem — will include config diff, deploy diff, and timeline.

ben: ETA for fix: 48-72h, will target a small patch to batch-key before next deploy.

support-oncall: Thanks all.
